kind: SH2ZAM placement model: Yabause isolated SH-2 interpreter plus a harness SH7604 cache and region-cost model, not Saturn timing
cycleUnit: upstream interpreter per-opcode modeled cycles plus harness stall cycles (SH-2 clocks)
calibration: Region costs are taken from hardware notes of a Saturn port (2026-11-12), which cite Sega's Saturn programming FAQ for work RAM and an emulator's commented bus table for VDP1/VDP2; cartridge figures are ASSUMED there. None is measured by this project. The calibration image (saturn/benchmarks/yaul/calibration) times cached and cache-through loads from each work RAM and a RAM cartridge, which would check the fill and access costs; it has not been run.

hwram.basis: hardware notes of a Saturn port, 2026-11-12: fill about 7, write 4 a longword (byte and word writes ASSUMED the same)

lwram.basis: hardware notes of a Saturn port, 2026-11-12: 14 a longword (4 x 14 a line), 7 a word (byte ASSUMED as a word)

cart6.basis: ASSUMED: 6 clocks a 16-bit beat (low end of the 48-80 line range)

cart10.basis: ASSUMED: 10 clocks a 16-bit beat (high end of the 48-80 line range)

vdp1.basis: hardware notes of a Saturn port, 2026-11-12: 45 per VDP1 VRAM access, any size; cache-through

vdp2.basis: hardware notes of a Saturn port, 2026-11-12: 40 per VDP2 access, any size; cache-through

cacheModel: SH7604: 4 KB, 4 ways x 64 sets x 16-byte lines, true LRU, shared by instruction fetches and data, write-through, no write allocate. Read and fetch misses fill the line and stall for the region's fill cost; VDP1/VDP2 reads are cache-through and stall per access. Writes go through a one-entry write buffer: the next bus access waits for the previous write to finish. The cache sees the image's own addresses (set conflicts follow its layout); classes are per 16-byte line. Not modelled: the second SH-2 or DMA sharing the bus, SDRAM refresh or page effects, cache-through reads of work RAM or the cartridge (no figure for single reads), the on-chip divider's bus cost (its own model applies), two-way cache mode.

modes.warm: the cache as the previous call of the same kernel in the same fixture left it (the kernel in a loop with nothing in between); the first call starts empty
modes.cold: the cache empty at entry (every line the call touches costs one fill)
